Accepted PVE deviations

  • Section 4 (host firewall ufw) disabled: the HomeSecExplorer PVE9 guide § 1.1.1 recommends skipping benchmark CIS § 4 when the PVE firewall is enabled (harden-pve.yml § 1.2.4: enable=1, INPUT DROP, allow-list 8006/2222). deb13cis_section4: false + ufw purge are in group_vars/pve_nodes.yml / site.yml.
  • 2.1.13 rsync masked (not purged): dependency of the proxmox-ve meta-package (pve-apt-hook blocks its removal) — deb13cis_rsync_mask: true.
  • IPv4 forwarding / rp_filter kept: Proxmox acts as a router for its guests (SDN/NAT/PVE firewall) — deb13cis_is_router: true.

Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. Depending on your PAM configuration,\n# PAM authentication via KbdInteractiveAuthentication may bypass\n# the setting of \"PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\".\n# If you just want the PAM account and session checks to run without\n# PAM authentication, then enable this but set PasswordAuthentication\n# and KbdInteractiveAuthentication to 'no'.\nUsePAM yes\n\n#AllowAgentForwarding yes\n#AllowTcpForwarding yes\n#GatewayPorts no\n# X11Forwarding no\n#X11DisplayOffset 10\n#X11UseLocalhost yes\n#PermitTTY yes\nPrintMotd no\n#PrintLastLog yes\n#TCPKeepAlive yes\nPermitUserEnvironment no\n#Compression delayed\n#ClientAliveInterval 0\n#ClientAliveCountMax 3\n#UseDNS no\n#PidFile /run/sshd.pid\nMaxStartups 10:30:60\n#PermitTunnel no\n#ChrootDirectory Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nClientAliveCountMax 3\nDisableForwarding yes\nKexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256\nMACs -hmac-md5,hmac-md5-96,hmac-ripemd160,hmac-sha1-96,umac-64@openssh.com,hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com,hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com,hmac-ripemd160-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com,umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\nLogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\nLoginGraceTime 60\nPermitRootLogin no\n#StrictModes yes\nMaxAuthTries 4\nMaxSessions 8\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\nHostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\nIgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. Depending on your PAM configuration,\n# PAM authentication via KbdInteractiveAuthentication may bypass\n# the setting of \"PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\".\n# If you just want the PAM account and session checks to run without\n# PAM authentication, then enable this but set PasswordAuthentication\n# and KbdInteractiveAuthentication to 'no'.\nUsePAM yes\n\n#AllowAgentForwarding yes\n#AllowTcpForwarding yes\n#GatewayPorts no\n# X11Forwarding no\n#X11DisplayOffset 10\n#X11UseLocalhost yes\n#PermitTTY yes\nPrintMotd no\n#PrintLastLog yes\n#TCPKeepAlive yes\nPermitUserEnvironment no\n#Compression delayed\n#ClientAliveInterval 0\n#ClientAliveCountMax 3\n#UseDNS no\n#PidFile /run/sshd.pid\nMaxStartups 10:30:60\n#PermitTunnel no\n#ChrootDirectory none\n#VersionAddendum none\n\n# no default banner path\nBanner /etc/issue.net\n\n# Allow client to pass locale and color environment variables\nAcceptEnv LANG LC_* COLORTERM NO_COLOR\n\n# override default of no subsystems\nSubsystem\tsftp\t/usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server\n\n# Example of overriding settings on a per-user basis\n#Match User anoncvs\n#\tX11Forwarding no\n#\tAllowTcpForwarding should contain a list of the authorization modules that define\n# the central access policy for use on the system. The default is to\n# only deny service to users whose accounts are expired in /etc/shadow.\n#\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n#\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\naccount\trequired pam_faillock.so \naccount\t[success=1 new_authtok_reqd=done default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so \n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\naccount\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\naccount\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"yescrypt\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"yescrypt\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\trequisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3\npassword\trequisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root use_authtok\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\npassword\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success /etc/login.defs - Configuration control definitions for the shadow package.\n#\n\n# REQUIRED for useradd/userdel/usermod\n# Directory where mailboxes reside, _or_ name of file, relative to the\n# home directory. If you _do_ define MAIL_DIR and MAIL_FILE,\n# MAIL_DIR takes precedence.\n#\n# Essentially:\n# - MAIL_DIR defines the location of users mail spool files\n# (for mbox use) by appending the username to MAIL_DIR as defined\n# below.\n# - MAIL_FILE defines the location of the users mail spool files as the\n# fully-qualified filename obtained by prepending the user home\n# directory before $MAIL_FILE\n#\n# NOTE: This is no more used for setting up users MAIL environment variable\n# which is, starting from shadow 4.0.12-1 in Debian, entirely the\n# job of the pam_mail PAM modules\n# See default PAM configuration files provided for\n# login, su, etc.\n#\n# This is a temporary situation: setting these variables will soon\n# move to /etc/default/useradd and the variables will then be\n# no more supported\nMAIL_DIR /var/mail\n#MAIL_FILE .mail\n\n#\n# Enable display of unknown usernames when login(1) failures are recorded.\n#\n# WARNING: Unknown usernames may become world readable.\n# See #290803 and #298773 for details about how this could become a security\n# concern\nLOG_UNKFAIL_ENAB\tno\n\n#\n# Enable logging of successful logins\n#\nLOG_OK_LOGINS\t\tno\n\n#\n# If defined, file which maps tty line to TERM environment parameter.\n# Each line of the file is in a format similar to \"vt100 tty01\".\n#\n#TTYTYPE_FILE\t/etc/ttytype\n\n#\n# If defined, file which inhibits all the usual chatter during the login\n# sequence. If a full pathname, then hushed mode will be enabled if the\n# user's name or shell are found in the file. If not a full pathname, then\n# hushed mode will be enabled if the file exists in the user's home directory.\n#\nHUSHLOGIN_FILE\t.hushlogin\n#HUSHLOGIN_FILE\t/etc/hushlogins\n\n#\n# *REQUIRED* The default PATH settings, for superuser and normal users.\n#\n# (they are minimal, add the rest in the shell startup files)\nENV_SUPATH\tPATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin\nENV_PATH\tPATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games\n\n#\n# Terminal permissions for terminals after login(1).\n# These settings are ignored for remote and other logins.\n#\n#\tTTYGROUP\tLogin tty will be assigned this group ownership.\n#\tTTYPERM\t\tLogin tty will be set to this permission.\n#\n#TTYGROUP\ttty\nTTYPERM\t\t0600\n\n#\n# Login configuration initializations:\n#\n#\tERASECHAR\tTerminal ERASE character ('\\010' = backspace).\n#\tKILLCHAR\tTerminal KILL character ('\\025' = CTRL/U).\n#\n# The ERASECHAR and KILLCHAR are used only on System V machines.\n#\nERASECHAR\t0177\nKILLCHAR\t025\n\n# HOME_MODE is used by useradd(8) and newusers(8) to set the mode for new\n# home directories.\nHOME_MODE\t0700\n\n#\n# Password aging controls:\n#\n#\tPASS_MAX_DAYS\tMaximum number of days a password may be used.\n#\tPASS_MIN_DAYS\tMinimum number of days allowed between password changes.\n#\tPASS_WARN_AGE\tNumber of days warning given before a password expires.\n#\nPASS_MAX_DAYS 365\nPASS_MIN_DAYS 1\nPASS_WARN_AGE 7\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic uid selection in useradd(8)\n#\nUID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nUID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_UID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_UID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user uids\nSUB_UID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_UID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_UID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic gid selection in groupadd(8)\n#\nGID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nGID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_GID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_GID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user group ids\nSUB_GID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_GID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_GID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Max number of login(1) retries if password is bad\n# This will most likely be overriden by PAM, since the default pam_unix module\n# has it's own built in of 3 retries. However, this is a safe fallback in case\n# you are using an authentication module that does not enforce PAM_MAXTRIES.\n#\nLOGIN_RETRIES\t\t5\n\n#\n# Max time in seconds for login(1)\n#\nLOGIN_TIMEOUT\t\t60\n\n#\n# Which fields may be changed by regular users using chfn(1) - use\n# any combination of letters \"frwh\" (full name, room number, work\n# phone, home phone). If not defined, no changes are allowed.\n# For backward compatibility, \"yes\" = \"rwh\" and \"no\" = \"frwh\".\n#\nCHFN_RESTRICT\t\trwh\n\n#\n# If set to MD5, MD5-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA256, SHA256-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA512, SHA512-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to BCRYPT, BCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to YESCRYPT, YESCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to DES, DES-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password (default)\n# MD5 and DES should not be used for new hashes, see crypt(5) for recommendations.\n# Overrides the MD5_CRYPT_ENAB option\n#\n# Note: It is recommended to use a value consistent with\n# the PAM modules configuration.\n#\nENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT\n\n#\n# Should login be allowed if we can't cd to the home directory?\n# Default is no.\n#\nDEFAULT_HOME\tyes\n\n#\n# The pwck(8) utility emits a warning for any system account with a home\n# directory that does not exist. Some system accounts intentionally do\n# not have a home directory. Such accounts may have this string as\n# their home directory in /etc/passwd to avoid a spurious warning.\n#\nNONEXISTENT\t/nonexistent\n\n#\n# If defined, this command is run when removing a user.\n# It should remove any at/cron/print jobs etc. owned by\n# the user to be removed (passed as the first argument).\n#\n#USERDEL_CMD\t/usr/sbin/userdel_local\n\n#\n# If set to yes, userdel(8) will remove the user's group if it contains no more\n# members, and useradd(8) will create by default a group with the name of the\n# user.\n#\n# Other former uses of this variable are not used in PAM environments, such as\n# Debian.\n#\nUSERGROUPS_ENAB yes\nUMASK 027\n", "expected": [ "/^PASS_MIN_DAYS\\s[1-9]/", "!/^PASS_MIN_DAYS\\s0/" ], "extra-elements": null, "found-elements": null, "message": every possible option\n# For a complete reference, see man aide.conf(5)\n\n# set environment for executable config files included by x_include\n@@x_include_setenv UPAC_settingsd /etc/aide/aide.settings.d\n@@x_include_setenv PATH /bin:/usr/bin\n\n# The daily aide check job depends on these paths and settings\ndatabase_in=file:/var/lib/aide/aide.db\ndatabase_out=file:/var/lib/aide/aide.db.new\ndatabase_new=file:/var/lib/aide/aide.db.new\ngzip_dbout=yes\n\n# Set to no to disable report_summarize_changes option.\n#report_summarize_changes=true\n\n# Set to no to disable grouping of files in report.\n#report_grouped=true\n\n# have AIDE version and time of database generation in database\n#database_add_metadata=true\n\n# Set verbosity of aide run and reports\n#log_level=warning\n#report_level=changed_attributes\n\n# Ignore e2fs attributes that cannot be set manually\nreport_ignore_e2fsattrs=VNIE\n\n# Set to yes to print the checksums in the report in hex format\n#report_base16 = false\n\n###### GROUPS ######\n\n# See documentation in aide.conf(5). To list the default compount\n# groups available in this aide binary, use aide --version.\n\n# if you want to sacrifice security for speed, list some checksum\n# explicitly here. H specifies that all checksums compiled in are used.\nChecksums = H\n\n# The checksums of the databases to be printed in the report\n# Set to 'E' to disable. Set to a list if you want a special set of\n# checksums for the database itself\ndatabase_attrs = Checksums\n\nOwnerMode = p+u+g+ftype\nSize = s+b\nInodeData = OwnerMode+n+i+Size+l+X\nStaticFile = m+c+Checksums\nFull = InodeData+StaticFile\nVarTime = InodeData+Checksums\nVarInode = VarTime-i\nVarFile = OwnerMode+n+l+X\nVarDir = OwnerMode+n+i+X\nRecreatedDir = OwnerMode+n+X\nActiveDir = OwnerMode+i+X\nPidFile = VarFile\nLogDir = VarDir\n\n# Files that stay static but are copied to a ram disk on startup\n# (causing different inode). Please do not use for new rules.\nRamdiskData = InodeData-i\n\n# VarDirInode is kind of a misnomer, as it does _less_ checks than\n# VarDir. Renaming it would mean touching \u003e 40 rule files though.\n# Please use RecreatedDir for new rules.\nVarDirInode = RecreatedDir\n\n# Directories that change their mtimes or ctimes but not their contents\nVarDirTime = InodeData\n\n###### LOG HANDLING ######\n\n# For a detailed description of the challenges of handling logs with\n# aide, see the \"LOG HANDLING\" section in aide.conf(5).\n\nActLog = Full+growing+ANF+I\nRotLog = Full\nCompSerLog = Full+I+compressed\nMidlSerLog = Full+I\nLastSerLog = Full+ARF\n\n# Please note that these example rules need to be adapted to the logrotate\n# configuration for the log. Compression may be disabled or lead to a\n# different extension, the dateext option may be used, old logs might be\n# held in a different place, a log series does not necessarily need to be\n# compressed etc.\n\n# Please note that savelog rotates the live log to .0 and not to .1 as it\n# is logrotates (changeable) default.\n\n# Log Handling, old method. This causes false reports and is not\n# necessary any more since aide 0.18. Please consider migating your\n# log rules to the new method. The groups used in this method will be\n# removed after Debian trixie (but of course you can re-add them).\n#\nLog = OwnerMode+n+growing+s+X\nFreqRotLog = Log-growing-s\nLowLog = Log-growing-s\nLoSerMemberLog = Full+I+ANF\nSerMemberLog = Full+I\nHiSerMemberLog = Full+I+ARF\nLowDELog = SerMemberLog+ANF+ARF\nSerMemberDELog = Full+ANF\nLinkedLog = Log-n\n\n# include rules from /etc/aide/aide.conf.d, honoring the\n# file name restrictions that are common in Debian. Files with\n# the x bit set are executed and their output included.\n@@x_include /etc/aide/aide.conf.d ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$\n# BEGIN Audit tools - CIS benchmark - Ansible-lockdown\n/usr/sbin/auditctl configuration file. See\n# sshd_config(5) for more information.\n\n# This sshd was compiled with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/games\n\n# The strategy used for options in the default sshd_config shipped with\n# OpenSSH is to specify options with their default value where\n# possible, but leave them commented. Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nClientAliveCountMax 3\nDisableForwarding yes\nKexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256\nMACs -hmac-md5,hmac-md5-96,hmac-ripemd160,hmac-sha1-96,umac-64@openssh.com,hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com,hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com,hmac-ripemd160-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com,umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\nLogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\nLoginGraceTime 60\nPermitRootLogin no\n#StrictModes yes\nMaxAuthTries 4\nMaxSessions 8\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\nHostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\nIgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. If this is enabled, PAM authentication will\n# be allowed through the KbdInteractiveAuthentication and\n# PasswordAuthentication. Depending on your PAM configuration,\n# PAM authentication via KbdInteractiveAuthentication may bypass\n# the setting of \"PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\".\n# If you just want the PAM account and See\n# sshd_config(5) for more information.\n\n# This sshd was compiled with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/games\n\n# The strategy used for options in the default sshd_config shipped with\n# OpenSSH is to specify options with their default value where\n# possible, but leave them commented. Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nClientAliveCountMax 3\nDisableForwarding yes\nKexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256\nMACs -hmac-md5,hmac-md5-96,hmac-ripemd160,hmac-sha1-96,umac-64@openssh.com,hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com,hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com,hmac-ripemd160-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com,umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\nLogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\nLoginGraceTime 60\nPermitRootLogin no\n#StrictModes yes\nMaxAuthTries 4\nMaxSessions 8\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\nHostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\nIgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. "duration": 59523, "end-time": "2026-11-19T09:22:36.796330034+01:00", "err": null, "matcher-result": { "actual": "#\n# /etc/pam.d/common-password - password-related modules common to all services\n#\n# This file is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of modules that define the services to be\n# used to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"yescrypt\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"yescrypt\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\trequisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3\npassword\trequisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root use_authtok\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\npassword\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\npassword\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package modules (the \"Additional\" block)\n# end of pam-auth-update config\n", "expected": [ "/^\\s*password\\s+(required|requisite)\\s+pam_pwhistory.so/" ], "extra-elements": null, "found-elements": null, "message": "matches expectation", "missing-elements": null, "actual": "#\n# /etc/pam.d/common-password - password-related modules common to all services\n#\n# This file is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of modules that define the services to be\n# used to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"yescrypt\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"yescrypt\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\trequisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3\npassword\trequisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root use_authtok\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module "2026-11-19T09:22:36.799963452+01:00", "err": null, "matcher-result": { "actual": "#\n# /etc/login.defs - Configuration control definitions for the shadow package.\n#\n\n# REQUIRED for useradd/userdel/usermod\n# Directory where mailboxes reside, _or_ name of file, relative to the\n# home directory. If you _do_ define MAIL_DIR and MAIL_FILE,\n# MAIL_DIR takes precedence.\n#\n# Essentially:\n# - MAIL_DIR defines the location of users mail spool files\n# (for mbox use) by appending the username to MAIL_DIR as defined\n# below.\n# - MAIL_FILE defines the location of the users mail spool files as the\n# fully-qualified filename obtained by prepending the user home\n# directory before $MAIL_FILE\n#\n# NOTE: This is no more used for setting up users MAIL environment variable\n# which is, starting from shadow 4.0.12-1 in Debian, entirely the\n# job of the pam_mail PAM modules\n# See default PAM configuration files provided for\n# login, su, etc.\n#\n# This is a temporary situation: setting these variables will soon\n# move to /etc/default/useradd and the variables will then be\n# no more supported\nMAIL_DIR /var/mail\n#MAIL_FILE .mail\n\n#\n# Enable display of unknown usernames when login(1) failures are recorded.\n#\n# WARNING: Unknown usernames may become world readable.\n# See #290803 and #298773 for details about how this could become a security\n# concern\nLOG_UNKFAIL_ENAB\tno\n\n#\n# Enable logging of successful logins\n#\nLOG_OK_LOGINS\t\tno\n\n#\n# If defined, file which maps tty line to TERM environment parameter.\n# Each line of the file is in a format similar to \"vt100 tty01\".\n#\n#TTYTYPE_FILE\t/etc/ttytype\n\n#\n# If defined, file which inhibits all the usual chatter during the login\n# sequence. If a full pathname, then hushed mode will be enabled if the\n# user's name or shell are found in the file. If not a full pathname, then\n# hushed mode will be enabled if the file exists in the user's home directory.\n#\nHUSHLOGIN_FILE\t.hushlogin\n#HUSHLOGIN_FILE\t/etc/hushlogins\n\n#\n# *REQUIRED* The default PATH settings, for superuser and normal users.\n#\n# (they are minimal, add the rest in the shell startup files)\nENV_SUPATH\tPATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin\nENV_PATH\tPATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games\n\n#\n# Terminal permissions for terminals after login(1).\n# These settings are ignored for remote and other logins.\n#\n#\tTTYGROUP\tLogin tty will be assigned this group ownership.\n#\tTTYPERM\t\tLogin tty will be set to this permission.\n#\n#TTYGROUP\ttty\nTTYPERM\t\t0600\n\n#\n# Login configuration initializations:\n#\n#\tERASECHAR\tTerminal ERASE character ('\\010' = backspace).\n#\tKILLCHAR\tTerminal KILL character ('\\025' = CTRL/U).\n#\n# The ERASECHAR and KILLCHAR are used only on System V machines.\n#\nERASECHAR\t0177\nKILLCHAR\t025\n\n# HOME_MODE is used by useradd(8) and newusers(8) to set the mode for new\n# home directories.\nHOME_MODE\t0700\n\n#\n# Password aging controls:\n#\n#\tPASS_MAX_DAYS\tMaximum number of days a password may be used.\n#\tPASS_MIN_DAYS\tMinimum number of days allowed between password changes.\n#\tPASS_WARN_AGE\tNumber of days warning given before a password expires.\n#\nPASS_MAX_DAYS 365\nPASS_MIN_DAYS 1\nPASS_WARN_AGE 7\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic uid selection in useradd(8)\n#\nUID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nUID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_UID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_UID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user uids\nSUB_UID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_UID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_UID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic gid selection in groupadd(8)\n#\nGID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nGID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_GID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_GID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user group ids\nSUB_GID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_GID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_GID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Max number of login(1) retries if password is bad\n# This will most likely be overriden by PAM, since the default pam_unix module\n# has it's own built in of 3 retries. However, this is a safe fallback in case\n# you are using an authentication module that does not enforce PAM_MAXTRIES.\n#\nLOGIN_RETRIES\t\t5\n\n#\n# Max time in seconds for login(1)\n#\nLOGIN_TIMEOUT\t\t60\n\n#\n# Which fields may be changed by regular users using chfn(1) - use\n# any combination of letters \"frwh\" (full name, room number, work\n# phone, home phone). If not defined, no changes are allowed.\n# For backward compatibility, \"yes\" = \"rwh\" and \"no\" = \"frwh\".\n#\nCHFN_RESTRICT\t\trwh\n\n#\n# If set to MD5, MD5-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA256, SHA256-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA512, SHA512-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to BCRYPT, BCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to YESCRYPT, YESCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to DES, DES-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password (default)\n# MD5 and DES should not be used for new hashes, see crypt(5) for recommendations.\n# Overrides the MD5_CRYPT_ENAB option\n#\n# Note: It is recommended to use a value consistent with\n# the PAM modules configuration.\n#\nENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT\n\n#\n# Should login be allowed if we can't cd to the home directory?\n# Default is no.\n#\nDEFAULT_HOME\tyes\n\n#\n# The pwck(8) utility emits a warning for any system account with a home\n# directory that does not exist. Some system accounts intentionally do\n# not have a home directory. Such accounts may have this string as\n# their home directory in /etc/passwd to avoid a spurious warning.\n#\nNONEXISTENT\t/nonexistent\n\n#\n# If defined, this command is run when removing a user.\n# It should remove any at/cron/print jobs etc. owned by\n# the user to be removed (passed as the first argument).\n#\n#USERDEL_CMD\t/usr/sbin/userdel_local\n\n#\n# If set to yes, userdel(8) will remove the user's group if it contains no more\n# members, and useradd(8) will create by default a group with the name of the\n# user.\n#\n# Other former uses of this variable are not used in PAM See\n# sshd_config(5) for more information.\n\n# This sshd was compiled with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/games\n\n# The strategy used for options in the default sshd_config shipped with\n# OpenSSH is to specify options with their default value where\n# possible, but leave them commented. Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nClientAliveCountMax 3\nDisableForwarding yes\nKexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256\nMACs -hmac-md5,hmac-md5-96,hmac-ripemd160,hmac-sha1-96,umac-64@openssh.com,hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com,hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com,hmac-ripemd160-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com,umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\nLogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\nLoginGraceTime 60\nPermitRootLogin no\n#StrictModes yes\nMaxAuthTries 4\nMaxSessions 8\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\nHostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\nIgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. If this is enabled, PAM authentication will\n# be allowed through the KbdInteractiveAuthentication and\n# PasswordAuthentication. Depending on your PAM configuration,\n# PAM authentication via KbdInteractiveAuthentication may bypass\n# the setting of \"PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\".\n# If you just want the PAM account and session checks to run without\n# PAM authentication, then enable this but set PasswordAuthentication\n# and KbdInteractiveAuthentication to 'no'.\nUsePAM yes\n\n#AllowAgentForwarding yes\n#AllowTcpForwarding yes\n#GatewayPorts no\n# X11Forwarding no\n#X11DisplayOffset 10\n#X11UseLocalhost yes\n#PermitTTY yes\nPrintMotd no\n#PrintLastLog yes\n#TCPKeepAlive yes\nPermitUserEnvironment no\n#Compression delayed\n#ClientAliveInterval 0\n#ClientAliveCountMax 3\n#UseDNS no\n#PidFile /run/sshd.pid\nMaxStartups 10:30:60\n#PermitTunnel no\n#ChrootDirectory none\n#VersionAddendum none\n\n# no default banner path\nBanner /etc/issue.net\n\n# Allow client to pass locale and color environment variables\nAcceptEnv LANG LC_* COLORTERM NO_COLOR\n\n# override default of no subsystems\nSubsystem\tsftp\t/usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server\n\n# Example of overriding settings on a per-user basis\n#Match User anoncvs\n#\tX11Forwarding no\n#\tAllowTcpForwarding is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of modules that define the services to be\n# used to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"yescrypt\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"yescrypt\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\trequisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3\npassword\trequisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root use_authtok\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\npassword\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\npassword\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package modules (the \"Additional\" block)\n# end of pam-auth-update config\n", "expected": [ "/^\\s*password\\s+\\[success=\\d default=.*\\]\\s+pam_unix.so/" ], "extra-elements": null, "found-elements": null, "message": "matches expectation", "missing-elements": null, "actual": "#\n# /etc/pam.d/common-auth - authentication settings common to all services\n#\n# This file is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of the authentication modules that define\n# the central authentication scheme for use on the system\n# (e.g., /etc/shadow, LDAP, Kerberos, etc.). The default is to use the\n# traditional Unix authentication mechanisms.\n#\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\nauth\trequisite pam_faillock.so preauth\nauth\t[success=2 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so try_first_pass\nauth\t[default=die] pam_faillock.so authfail\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\nauth\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\nauth\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here member of \"foo\" or explicitly\n# permitted earlier by e.g. \"sufficient pam_rootok.so\").\n# (Replaces the `SU_WHEEL_ONLY' option from login.defs)\n# auth required pam_wheel.so\n\n# Uncomment this all.\n# auth required pam_wheel.so deny group=nosu\n\n# Uncomment and edit /etc/security/time.conf if you need to set\n# time restrainst on su usage.\n# (Replaces the `PORTTIME_CHECKS_ENAB' option MAIL_DIR and MAIL_FILE variables\n# in /etc/login.defs to make sure that removing a user \n# also removes the user's mail spool file.\n# See comments in /etc/login.defs\n#\n# \"nopen\" stands to avoid See\n# sshd_config(5) for more information.\n\n# This sshd was compiled with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/games\n\n# The strategy used for options in the default sshd_config shipped with\n# OpenSSH is to specify options with their default value where\n# possible, but leave them commented. Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nClientAliveCountMax 3\nDisableForwarding yes\nKexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256\nMACs -hmac-md5,hmac-md5-96,hmac-ripemd160,hmac-sha1-96,umac-64@openssh.com,hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com,hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com,hmac-ripemd160-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com,umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\nLogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\nLoginGraceTime 60\nPermitRootLogin no\n#StrictModes yes\nMaxAuthTries 4\nMaxSessions 8\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\nHostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\nIgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. If this is enabled, PAM authentication will\n# be allowed through the KbdInteractiveAuthentication and\n# PasswordAuthentication. Depending on your PAM configuration,\n# PAM authentication via KbdInteractiveAuthentication may bypass\n# the setting of \"PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\".\n# If you just want the PAM account and session checks to run without\n# PAM authentication, then enable this but set PasswordAuthentication\n# and KbdInteractiveAuthentication to 'no'.\nUsePAM yes\n\n#AllowAgentForwarding yes\n#AllowTcpForwarding yes\n#GatewayPorts no\n# X11Forwarding no\n#X11DisplayOffset 10\n#X11UseLocalhost yes\n#PermitTTY yes\nPrintMotd no\n#PrintLastLog yes\n#TCPKeepAlive yes\nPermitUserEnvironment no\n#Compression delayed\n#ClientAliveInterval 0\n#ClientAliveCountMax 3\n#UseDNS no\n#PidFile /run/sshd.pid\nMaxStartups 10:30:60\n#PermitTunnel no\n#ChrootDirectory none\n#VersionAddendum none\n\n# no default banner path\nBanner /etc/issue.net\n\n# Allow client to pass locale and color environment variables\nAcceptEnv LANG LC_* COLORTERM NO_COLOR\n\n# override default of no subsystems\nSubsystem\tsftp\t/usr/lib/openssh/sftp-server\n\n# Example of overriding settings on a per-user basis\n#Match User anoncvs\n#\tX11Forwarding no\n#\tAllowTcpForwarding service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of the authentication modules that define\n# the central authentication scheme for use on the system\n# (e.g., /etc/shadow, LDAP, Kerberos, etc.). The default is to use the\n# traditional Unix authentication mechanisms.\n#\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\nauth\trequisite pam_faillock.so preauth\nauth\t[success=2 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so try_first_pass\nauth\t[default=die] pam_faillock.so authfail\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\nauth\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\nauth\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package modules (the \"Additional\" block)\n# end of pam-auth-update config\n", "expected": [ "/^\\s*auth\\s+\\[success=\\d default=.*\\]\\s+pam_unix.so/" ], "extra-elements": null, The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"yescrypt\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"yescrypt\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\trequisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3\npassword\trequisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root use_authtok\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\npassword\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\npassword\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package modules (the \"Additional\" block)\n# end of pam-auth-update informative messages via syslog.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# no_log_info\n#\n# Only track failed user authentications attempts for local users\n# in /etc/passwd and ignore centralized (AD, IdM, LDAP, etc.) users.\n# The `faillock` command will also no longer track user failed\n# authentication attempts. Enabling this option will prevent a\n# double-lockout scenario where a user is locked out locally and\n# in the centralized mechanism.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# local_users_only\n#\n# Deny access if the number of consecutive authentication failures\n# for this user during the recent interval exceeds n tries.\n# The default is 3.\n# deny = 3\n#\n# The length of the interval during which the consecutive\n# authentication failures must happen for the user account\n# lock out is \u003creplaceable\u003en\u003c/replaceable\u003e seconds.\n# The default is 900 (15 minutes).\n# fail_interval = 900\n#\n# The access will be re-enabled after n seconds after the lock out.\n# The value 0 has the same meaning as value `never` - the access\n# will not be re-enabled without resetting the faillock\n# entries by the `faillock` command.\n# The default is 600 (10 minutes).\n# unlock_time = 600\n#\n# Root account can become locked as well as regular accounts.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# even_deny_root\n#\n# This option implies the `even_deny_root` option.\n# Allow access after n seconds to root account after the\n# account is locked. In case the option is not specified\n# the value is the same as of the `unlock_time` option.\n# root_unlock_time = 900\n#\n# If a group name is specified with this option, members\n# of the group will be handled by this module the same as\n# the root account (the options `even_deny_root\u003e` and\n# `root_unlock_time` will apply to them.\n# By default, the option is not set.\n# admin_group = Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nClientAliveCountMax 3\nDisableForwarding yes\nKexAlgorithms mlkem768x25519-sha256,sntrup761x25519-sha512,ecdh-sha2-nistp256,ecdh-sha2-nistp384,ecdh-sha2-nistp521,diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512,diffie-hellman-group18-sha512,diffie-hellman-group14-sha256\nMACs -hmac-md5,hmac-md5-96,hmac-ripemd160,hmac-sha1-96,umac-64@openssh.com,hmac-md5-etm@openssh.com,hmac-md5-96-etm@openssh.com,hmac-ripemd160-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha1-96-etm@openssh.com,umac-64-etm@openssh.com,umac-128-etm@openssh.com\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\nLogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\nLoginGraceTime 60\nPermitRootLogin no\n#StrictModes yes\nMaxAuthTries 4\nMaxSessions 8\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\nHostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\nIgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\nPermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Depending on\n# the system's configuration, this may involve passwords, challenge-response,\n# one-time passwords or some combination of these and other methods.\n# Beware issues with some PAM modules and threads.\nKbdInteractiveAuthentication no\n\n# Kerberos options\n#KerberosAuthentication no\n#KerberosOrLocalPasswd yes\n#KerberosTicketCleanup yes\n#KerberosGetAFSToken no\n\n# GSSAPI options\nGSSAPIAuthentication no\n#GSSAPICleanupCredentials yes\n#GSSAPIStrictAcceptorCheck yes\n#GSSAPIKeyExchange no\n\n# Set this to 'yes' to enable PAM authentication, account processing,\n# and session processing. Depending on your PAM configuration,\n# PAM authentication via KbdInteractiveAuthentication may bypass\n# the setting of \"PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\".\n# If you just want the PAM account and session checks to run without\n# PAM authentication, then enable this but set PasswordAuthentication\n# and KbdInteractiveAuthentication to 'no'.\nUsePAM yes\n\n#AllowAgentForwarding The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"yescrypt\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"yescrypt\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\trequisite pam_pwquality.so retry=3\npassword\trequisite pam_pwhistory.so remember=24 enforce_for_root use_authtok\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure use_authtok try_first_pass yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\npassword\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\npassword\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package modules (the \"Additional\" block)\n# end of pam-auth-update config\n", "expected": [ "/^\\s*password\\s*(requisite|required)\\s*pam_pwhistory.so.*remember\\s*=\\s*(2[4-9]|[3-9][0-9])/" ], "extra-elements": null, "found-elements": null, "message": "matches See chrony.conf(5) for more\n# information about usable directives.\n\n# Use Debian vendor zone.\npool 2.debian.pool.ntp.org iburst\n\n# Use time sources from DHCP.\nsourcedir /run/chrony-dhcp\n\n# Use NTP sources found in /etc/chrony/sources.d.\nsourcedir /etc/chrony/sources.d\n\n# This directive specifies the location of the file containing ID/key pairs for\n# NTP authentication.\nkeyfile /etc/chrony/chrony.keys\n\n# This directive specifies the file into which chronyd will store the rate\n# information.\ndriftfile /var/lib/chrony/chrony.drift\n\n# Save NTS keys and cookies.\nntsdumpdir /var/lib/chrony\n\n# Uncomment the following line to turn logging on.\n#log tracking measurements statistics\n\n# Log files location.\nlogdir /var/log/chrony\n\n# Stop bad estimates upsetting machine clock.\nmaxupdateskew 100.0\n\n# This directive enables kernel synchronisation (every 11 minutes) of the\n# real-time clock. Note that it can't be used along with the 'rtcfile' directive.\nrtcsync\n\n# Step the system clock instead of slewing it if the adjustment is larger than\n# one second, but only in the first three clock updates.\nmakestep 1 3\n\n# Get TAI-UTC offset and leap seconds from the system tz database.\n# This directive must be commented out when using time sources serving\n# leap-smeared time.\nleapseclist /usr/share/zoneinfo/leap-seconds.list\n\n# Include configuration files found in /etc/chrony/conf.d.\nconfdir /etc/chrony/conf.d\nuser _chrony\n", "expected": [ "/^user _chrony/" ], central access policy for use on the system. The default is to\n# only deny service to users whose accounts are expired in /etc/shadow.\n#\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. "matcher-result": { "actual": "# Configuration for locking the user after multiple failed\n# authentication attempts.\n#\n# The directory where the user files with the failure records are kept.\n# The default is /var/run/faillock.\n# dir = /var/run/faillock\n#\n# Will log the user name into the system log if the user is not found.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# audit\n#\n# Don't print informative messages.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# silent\n#\n# Don't log informative messages via syslog.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# no_log_info\n#\n# Only track failed user authentications attempts for local users\n# in /etc/passwd and ignore centralized (AD, IdM, LDAP, etc.) users.\n# The `faillock` command will also no longer track user failed\n# authentication attempts. /etc/pam.d/common-password - password-related modules common to all services\n#\n# This file is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of modules that define the services to be\n# used to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"sha512\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"sha512\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. See the pam_unix manpage\n#for other options.\n\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. See\n# pam-auth-update(8) for details.\n\n# here are the per-package modules (the \"Primary\" block)\npassword\t[success=1 default=ignore]\tpam_unix.so obscure yescrypt\n# here's the fallback if no module succeeds\npassword\trequisite\t\t\tpam_deny.so\n# prime the stack with a positive return value if there isn't one already;\n# this avoids us returning an error just because nothing sets a success code\n# since the modules above will each just jump around\npassword\trequired\t\t\tpam_permit.so\n# and here are more per-package modules (the \"Additional\" block)\n# end of pam-auth-update "actual": "#\n# /etc/pam.d/common-password - password-related modules common to all services\n#\n# This file is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of modules that define the services to be\n# used to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Prior releases\n#used the option \"sha512\"; if a shadow password hash will be shared\n#between Debian 11 and older releases replace \"yescrypt\" with \"sha512\"\n#for compatibility . The \"obscure\" option replaces the old\n#`OBSCURE_CHECKS_ENAB' option in login.defs. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. "actual": "# Configuration for locking the user after multiple failed\n# authentication attempts.\n#\n# The directory where the user files with the failure records are kept.\n# The default is /var/run/faillock.\n# dir = /var/run/faillock\n#\n# Will log the user name into the system log if the user is not found.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# audit\n#\n# Don't print informative messages.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# silent\n#\n# Don't log informative messages via syslog.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# no_log_info\n#\n# Only track failed user authentications attempts for local users\n# in /etc/passwd and ignore centralized (AD, IdM, LDAP, etc.) users.\n# The `faillock` command will also no longer track user failed\n# authentication attempts. Enabling this option will prevent a\n# double-lockout scenario where a user is locked out locally and\n# in the centralized mechanism.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# local_users_only\n#\n# Deny access if the number of consecutive authentication failures\n# for this user during the recent interval exceeds n tries.\n# The default is 3.\n# deny = 3\n#\n# The length of the interval during which the consecutive\n# authentication failures must happen for the user account\n# lock out is \u003creplaceable\u003en\u003c/replaceable\u003e seconds.\n# The default is 900 (15 minutes).\n# fail_interval = 900\n#\n# The access will be re-enabled after n seconds after the lock out.\n# The value 0 has the same meaning as value `never` - the access\n# will not be re-enabled without resetting the faillock\n# entries by the `faillock` command.\n# The default is 600 (10 minutes).\n# unlock_time = 600\n#\n# Root account can become locked as well as regular accounts.\n# Enabled if option is present.\n# even_deny_root\n#\n# This option implies the `even_deny_root` option.\n# Allow access after n seconds to root account after the\n# account is locked. Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\n#LogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\n#LoginGraceTime 2m\n#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\n#StrictModes yes\n#MaxAuthTries 6\n#MaxSessions 10\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\n#HostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\n#IgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\n#PermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. { "duration": 36528, "end-time": "2026-11-19T09:01:49.595504923+01:00", "err": null, "matcher-result": { "actual": "#\n# /etc/login.defs - Configuration control definitions for the shadow package.\n#\n\n# REQUIRED for useradd/userdel/usermod\n# Directory where mailboxes reside, _or_ name of file, relative to the\n# home directory. If you _do_ define MAIL_DIR and MAIL_FILE,\n# MAIL_DIR takes precedence.\n#\n# Essentially:\n# - MAIL_DIR defines the location of users mail spool files\n# (for mbox use) by appending the username to MAIL_DIR as defined\n# below.\n# - MAIL_FILE defines the location of the users mail spool files as the\n# fully-qualified filename obtained by prepending the user home\n# directory before $MAIL_FILE\n#\n# NOTE: This is no more used for setting up users MAIL environment variable\n# which is, starting from shadow 4.0.12-1 in Debian, entirely the\n# job of the pam_mail PAM modules\n# See default PAM configuration files provided for\n# login, su, etc.\n#\n# This is a temporary situation: setting these variables will soon\n# move to /etc/default/useradd and the variables will then be\n# no more supported\nMAIL_DIR /var/mail\n#MAIL_FILE .mail\n\n#\n# Enable display of unknown usernames when login(1) failures are recorded.\n#\n# WARNING: Unknown usernames may become world readable.\n# See #290803 and #298773 for details about how this could become a security\n# concern\nLOG_UNKFAIL_ENAB\tno\n\n#\n# Enable logging of successful logins\n#\nLOG_OK_LOGINS\t\tno\n\n#\n# If defined, file which maps tty line to TERM environment parameter.\n# Each line of the file is in a format similar to \"vt100 tty01\".\n#\n#TTYTYPE_FILE\t/etc/ttytype\n\n#\n# If defined, file which inhibits all the usual chatter during the login\n# sequence. If a full pathname, then hushed mode will be enabled if the\n# user's name or shell are found in the file. If not a full pathname, then\n# hushed mode will be enabled if the file exists in the user's home directory.\n#\nHUSHLOGIN_FILE\t.hushlogin\n#HUSHLOGIN_FILE\t/etc/hushlogins\n\n#\n# *REQUIRED* The default PATH settings, for superuser and normal users.\n#\n# (they are minimal, add the rest in the shell startup files)\nENV_SUPATH\tPATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin\nENV_PATH\tPATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games\n\n#\n# Terminal permissions for terminals after login(1).\n# These settings are ignored for remote and other logins.\n#\n#\tTTYGROUP\tLogin tty will be assigned this group ownership.\n#\tTTYPERM\t\tLogin tty will be set to this permission.\n#\n#TTYGROUP\ttty\nTTYPERM\t\t0600\n\n#\n# Login configuration initializations:\n#\n#\tERASECHAR\tTerminal ERASE character ('\\010' = backspace).\n#\tKILLCHAR\tTerminal KILL character ('\\025' = CTRL/U).\n#\n# The ERASECHAR and KILLCHAR are used only on System V machines.\n#\nERASECHAR\t0177\nKILLCHAR\t025\n\n# HOME_MODE is used by useradd(8) and newusers(8) to set the mode for new\n# home directories.\nHOME_MODE\t0700\n\n#\n# Password aging controls:\n#\n#\tPASS_MAX_DAYS\tMaximum number of days a password may be used.\n#\tPASS_MIN_DAYS\tMinimum number of days allowed between password changes.\n#\tPASS_WARN_AGE\tNumber of days warning given before a password expires.\n#\nPASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999\nPASS_MIN_DAYS\t0\nPASS_WARN_AGE\t7\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic should contain a list of modules that define tasks to be performed\n# at the start and end of interactive sessions.\n#\n# As of pam 1.0.1-6, this file is managed by pam-auth-update by default.\n# To take advantage of this, it is recommended that you configure any\n# local modules either before or after the default block, and use\n# pam-auth-update to manage selection of other modules. "#\n# /etc/login.defs - Configuration control definitions for the shadow package.\n#\n\n# REQUIRED for useradd/userdel/usermod\n# Directory where mailboxes reside, _or_ name of file, relative to the\n# home directory. If you _do_ define MAIL_DIR and MAIL_FILE,\n# MAIL_DIR takes precedence.\n#\n# Essentially:\n# - MAIL_DIR defines the location of users mail spool files\n# (for mbox use) by appending the username to MAIL_DIR as defined\n# below.\n# - MAIL_FILE defines the location of the users mail spool files as the\n# fully-qualified filename obtained by prepending the user home\n# directory before $MAIL_FILE\n#\n# NOTE: This is no more used for setting up users MAIL environment variable\n# which is, starting from shadow 4.0.12-1 in Debian, entirely the\n# job of the pam_mail PAM modules\n# See default PAM configuration files provided for\n# login, su, etc.\n#\n# This is a temporary situation: setting these variables will soon\n# move to /etc/default/useradd and the variables will then be\n# no more supported\nMAIL_DIR /var/mail\n#MAIL_FILE .mail\n\n#\n# Enable display of unknown usernames when login(1) failures are recorded.\n#\n# WARNING: Unknown usernames may become world readable.\n# See #290803 and #298773 for details about how this could become a security\n# concern\nLOG_UNKFAIL_ENAB\tno\n\n#\n# Enable logging of successful logins\n#\nLOG_OK_LOGINS\t\tno\n\n#\n# If defined, file which maps tty line to TERM environment parameter.\n# Each line of the file is in a format similar to \"vt100 tty01\".\n#\n#TTYTYPE_FILE\t/etc/ttytype\n\n#\n# If defined, file which inhibits all the usual chatter during the login\n# sequence. If a full pathname, then hushed mode will be enabled if the\n# user's name or shell are found in the file. If not a full pathname, then\n# hushed mode will be enabled if the file exists in the user's home directory.\n#\nHUSHLOGIN_FILE\t.hushlogin\n#HUSHLOGIN_FILE\t/etc/hushlogins\n\n#\n# *REQUIRED* The default PATH settings, for superuser and normal users.\n#\n# (they are minimal, add the rest in the shell startup files)\nENV_SUPATH\tPATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin\nENV_PATH\tPATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games\n\n#\n# Terminal permissions for terminals after login(1).\n# These settings are ignored for remote and other logins.\n#\n#\tTTYGROUP\tLogin tty will be assigned this group ownership.\n#\tTTYPERM\t\tLogin tty will be set to this permission.\n#\n#TTYGROUP\ttty\nTTYPERM\t\t0600\n\n#\n# Login configuration initializations:\n#\n#\tERASECHAR\tTerminal ERASE character ('\\010' = backspace).\n#\tKILLCHAR\tTerminal KILL character ('\\025' = CTRL/U).\n#\n# The ERASECHAR and KILLCHAR are used only on System V machines.\n#\nERASECHAR\t0177\nKILLCHAR\t025\n\n# HOME_MODE is used by useradd(8) and newusers(8) to set the mode for new\n# home directories.\nHOME_MODE\t0700\n\n#\n# Password aging controls:\n#\n#\tPASS_MAX_DAYS\tMaximum number of days a password may be used.\n#\tPASS_MIN_DAYS\tMinimum number of days allowed between password changes.\n#\tPASS_WARN_AGE\tNumber of days warning given before a password expires.\n#\nPASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999\nPASS_MIN_DAYS\t0\nPASS_WARN_AGE\t7\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic uid selection in useradd(8)\n#\nUID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nUID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_UID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_UID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user uids\nSUB_UID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_UID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_UID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic gid selection in groupadd(8)\n#\nGID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nGID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_GID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_GID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user group ids\nSUB_GID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_GID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_GID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Max number of login(1) retries if password is bad\n# This will most likely be overriden by PAM, since the default pam_unix module\n# has it's own built in of 3 retries. However, this is a safe fallback in case\n# you are using an authentication module that does not enforce PAM_MAXTRIES.\n#\nLOGIN_RETRIES\t\t5\n\n#\n# Max time in seconds for login(1)\n#\nLOGIN_TIMEOUT\t\t60\n\n#\n# Which fields may be changed by regular users using chfn(1) - use\n# any combination of letters \"frwh\" (full name, room number, work\n# phone, home phone). If not defined, no changes are allowed.\n# For backward compatibility, \"yes\" = \"rwh\" and \"no\" = \"frwh\".\n#\nCHFN_RESTRICT\t\trwh\n\n#\n# If set to MD5, MD5-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA256, SHA256-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA512, SHA512-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to BCRYPT, BCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to YESCRYPT, YESCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to DES, DES-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password (default)\n# MD5 and DES should not be used for new hashes, see crypt(5) for recommendations.\n# Overrides the MD5_CRYPT_ENAB option\n#\n# Note: It is recommended to use a value consistent with\n# the PAM modules configuration.\n#\nENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT\n\n#\n# Should login be allowed if we can't cd to the home directory?\n# Default is no.\n#\nDEFAULT_HOME\tyes\n\n#\n# The pwck(8) utility emits a warning for any system account with a home\n# directory that does not exist. Some system accounts intentionally do\n# not have a home directory. Such accounts may have this string as\n# their home directory in /etc/passwd to avoid a spurious warning.\n#\nNONEXISTENT\t/nonexistent\n\n#\n# If defined, this command is run when removing a user.\n# It should remove any at/cron/print jobs etc. owned by\n# the user to be removed (passed as the first argument).\n#\n#USERDEL_CMD\t/usr/sbin/userdel_local\n\n#\n# If set to yes, userdel(8) will remove the user's group if it contains no more\n# members, and useradd(8) will create by default a group with the name of the\n# user.\n#\n# Other former uses of this variable are not used in PAM environments, such as\n# Debian.\n#\nUSERGROUPS_ENAB yes\n", "expected": [ "/^ENCRYPT_METHOD (SHA512|YESCRYPT)/" ], "extra-elements": null, "found-elements": null, "message": "matches expectation", services\n#\n# This file is included from other service-specific PAM config files,\n# and should contain a list of modules that define the services to be\n# used to change user passwords. The default is pam_unix.\n\n# Explanation of pam_unix options:\n# The \"yescrypt\" option enables\n#hashed passwords using the yescrypt algorithm, introduced in Debian\n#11. Without this option, the default is Unix crypt. Uncommented options override the\n# default value.\n\nInclude /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf\n\n#Port 22\n#AddressFamily any\n#ListenAddress 0.0.0.0\n#ListenAddress ::\n\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key\n#HostKey /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key\n\n# Ciphers and keying\n#RekeyLimit default none\n\n# Logging\n#SyslogFacility AUTH\n#LogLevel INFO\n\n# Authentication:\n\n#LoginGraceTime 2m\n#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password\n#StrictModes yes\n#MaxAuthTries 6\n#MaxSessions 10\n\n#PubkeyAuthentication yes\n\n# Expect .ssh/authorized_keys2 to be disregarded by default in future.\n#AuthorizedKeysFile\t.ssh/authorized_keys .ssh/authorized_keys2\n\n#AuthorizedPrincipalsFile none\n\n#AuthorizedKeysCommand none\n#AuthorizedKeysCommandUser nobody\n\n# For this to work you will also need host keys in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts\n#HostbasedAuthentication no\n# Change to yes if you don't trust ~/.ssh/known_hosts for\n# HostbasedAuthentication\n#IgnoreUserKnownHosts no\n# Don't read the user's ~/.rhosts and ~/.shosts files\n#IgnoreRhosts yes\n\n# To disable tunneled clear text passwords, change to \"no\" here!\n#PasswordAuthentication yes\n#PermitEmptyPasswords no\n\n# Change to \"yes\" to enable keyboard-interactive authentication. Configuration control definitions for the shadow package.\n#\n\n# REQUIRED for useradd/userdel/usermod\n# Directory where mailboxes reside, _or_ name of file, relative to the\n# home directory. If you _do_ define MAIL_DIR and MAIL_FILE,\n# MAIL_DIR takes precedence.\n#\n# Essentially:\n# - MAIL_DIR defines the location of users mail spool files\n# (for mbox use) by appending the username to MAIL_DIR as defined\n# below.\n# - MAIL_FILE defines the location of the users mail spool files as the\n# fully-qualified filename obtained by prepending the user home\n# directory before $MAIL_FILE\n#\n# NOTE: This is no more used for setting up users MAIL environment variable\n# which is, starting from shadow 4.0.12-1 in Debian, entirely the\n# job of the pam_mail PAM modules\n# See default PAM configuration files provided for\n# login, su, etc.\n#\n# This is a temporary situation: setting these variables will soon\n# move to /etc/default/useradd and the variables will then be\n# no more supported\nMAIL_DIR /var/mail\n#MAIL_FILE .mail\n\n#\n# Enable display of unknown usernames when login(1) failures are recorded.\n#\n# WARNING: Unknown usernames may become world readable.\n# See #290803 and #298773 for details about how this could become a security\n# concern\nLOG_UNKFAIL_ENAB\tno\n\n#\n# Enable logging of successful logins\n#\nLOG_OK_LOGINS\t\tno\n\n#\n# If defined, file which maps tty line to TERM environment parameter.\n# Each line of the file is in a format similar to \"vt100 tty01\".\n#\n#TTYTYPE_FILE\t/etc/ttytype\n\n#\n# If defined, file which inhibits all the usual chatter during the login\n# sequence. If a full pathname, then hushed mode will be enabled if the\n# user's name or shell are found in the file. If not a full pathname, then\n# hushed mode will be enabled if the file exists in the user's home directory.\n#\nHUSHLOGIN_FILE\t.hushlogin\n#HUSHLOGIN_FILE\t/etc/hushlogins\n\n#\n# *REQUIRED* The default PATH settings, for superuser and normal users.\n#\n# (they are minimal, add the rest in the shell startup files)\nENV_SUPATH\tPATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin\nENV_PATH\tPATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games\n\n#\n# Terminal permissions for terminals after login(1).\n# These settings are ignored for remote and other logins.\n#\n#\tTTYGROUP\tLogin tty will be assigned this group ownership.\n#\tTTYPERM\t\tLogin tty will be set to this ('\\025' = CTRL/U).\n#\n# The ERASECHAR and KILLCHAR are used only on System V machines.\n#\nERASECHAR\t0177\nKILLCHAR\t025\n\n# HOME_MODE is used by useradd(8) and newusers(8) to set the mode for new\n# home directories.\nHOME_MODE\t0700\n\n#\n# Password aging controls:\n#\n#\tPASS_MAX_DAYS\tMaximum number of days a password may be used.\n#\tPASS_MIN_DAYS\tMinimum number of days allowed between password changes.\n#\tPASS_WARN_AGE\tNumber of days warning given before a password expires.\n#\nPASS_MAX_DAYS\t99999\nPASS_MIN_DAYS\t0\nPASS_WARN_AGE\t7\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic uid selection in useradd(8)\n#\nUID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nUID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_UID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_UID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user uids\nSUB_UID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_UID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_UID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Min/max values for automatic gid selection in groupadd(8)\n#\nGID_MIN\t\t\t 1000\nGID_MAX\t\t\t60000\n# System accounts\n#SYS_GID_MIN\t\t 101\n#SYS_GID_MAX\t\t 999\n# Extra per user group ids\nSUB_GID_MIN\t\t 100000\nSUB_GID_MAX\t\t600100000\nSUB_GID_COUNT\t\t 65536\n\n#\n# Max number of login(1) retries if However, this is a safe fallback in case\n# you are using an authentication module that does not enforce PAM_MAXTRIES.\n#\nLOGIN_RETRIES\t\t5\n\n#\n# Max time in seconds for login(1)\n#\nLOGIN_TIMEOUT\t\t60\n\n#\n# Which fields may be changed by regular users using chfn(1) - use\n# any combination of letters \"frwh\" (full name, room number, work\n# phone, home phone). If not defined, no changes are allowed.\n# For backward compatibility, \"yes\" = \"rwh\" and \"no\" = \"frwh\".\n#\nCHFN_RESTRICT\t\trwh\n\n#\n# If set to MD5, MD5-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA256, SHA256-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to SHA512, SHA512-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to BCRYPT, BCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to YESCRYPT, YESCRYPT-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password\n# If set to DES, DES-based algorithm will be used for encrypting password (default)\n# MD5 and DES should not be used for new hashes, see crypt(5) for recommendations.\n# Overrides the MD5_CRYPT_ENAB option\n#\n# Note: It is recommended to use a value consistent with\n# the PAM modules configuration.\n#\nENCRYPT_METHOD YESCRYPT\n\n#\n# Should login be allowed if we can't cd to the home directory?\n# Default is no.\n#\nDEFAULT_HOME\tyes\n\n#\n# The pwck(8) utility emits a warning for any system account with a home\n# directory that does not exist. Some system accounts intentionally do\n# not have a home directory. Such accounts may have this string as\n# their home directory in /etc/passwd to avoid a spurious warning.\n#\nNONEXISTENT\t/nonexistent\n\n#\n# If defined, this command is run when removing a user.\n# See\n# sshd_config(5) for more information.\n\n# This sshd was compiled with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/games\n\n# The strategy used for options in the default sshd_config shipped with\n# OpenSSH is to specify options with their default value where\n# possible, but leave them commented. member of \"foo\" or explicitly\n# permitted earlier by e.g. \"sufficient pam_rootok.so\").\n# (Replaces the `SU_WHEEL_ONLY' option from login.defs)\n# auth required pam_wheel.so\n\n# Uncomment this
